login.title: Sign in to AI-Biostat
login.intro: Pilot study: your participant code and password are issued by the teacher. No personal data needed.
login.passwordPh: 6 digits from the teacher or your own password
login.hint: Enter your participant code and password
login.tooMany: Too many attempts. Please wait 10 minutes

profile.title: Profile
profile.privacy: Your name is visible only to you and the teacher. Research exports use the code only.

password.title: Change password
password.intro: Set a password that is easy to remember — at least 6 characters, letters and digits allowed.
password.tooShort: New password must be at least 6 characters
password.done: Password changed. Use the new password next time you sign in.

diag.note: Correct answers are not shown — this is an assessment, not an exam. You can close it and come back to this question.
diag.growth: Area for growth — “{{weak}}”. The tutor will ask more questions on this topic.
diag.exitNote: This is the entry diagnostic: it is taken once. The final one (variant B) will be opened by your teacher at the end of the pilot.
diag.exitOpenTitle: Your teacher has opened the final diagnostic
diag.exitOpenText: 20 questions like at the start, but different ones. Afterwards you will see how your results have changed.
diag.compareLead: Entry (variant A) and final (variant B) diagnostic across the four competencies.
diag.exitDone: Final diagnostic completed. Thank you for taking part in the pilot!

home.fillProfile: Add your name in the profile so the teacher can see whose work this is.
home.footer: All pilot cases contain training data only. The other 25 catalogue cases come after the pilot.

player.lockedNote: Method chosen: steps 1–4 are now read-only.
player.eduText: The data were simulated for this training task and contain no real information about patients, healthcare organisations or territories.

save.expired: Session expired — please sign in again
save.offline: No connection — answers will be saved when it is restored

tutor.title: AI tutor
tutor.blocked4: Answer on your own first — the tutor is not used at the “Question” step.
tutor.blocked7: You write the conclusion yourself. The tutor is not used at this step.
tutor.blocked8: Here you are checking an AI, so the tutor is not available.
tutor.intro: In the pilot the tutor opens in a separate tab. Your answers and scores are saved only here, in AI-Biostat.
tutor.how1: Copy a question below or ask your own
tutor.how3: Come back to this tab — your step is saved
tutor.askHere: What you can ask at this step
tutor.defaultQ: How should I approach this step?
tutor.counter: Tutor visits: {{n}} · counted in the study

step2.title: Step 2. Exploring the data
step2.intro: Check the data before the analysis. Click the rows that contain errors.
step2.why: Mark at least one row with an error

step3.title: Step 3. Variable types
step3.intro: Set the type of each variable and mark the outcome — what we are explaining.
step3.why: Set the type of all {{n}} variables and mark the outcome

step4.title: Step 4. Research question
step4.intro: State the research question and hypothesis in your own words. The tutor is not available at this step.
step4.label: Question and hypothesis
step4.why: Write at least one sentence (6+ words)

step5.title: Step 5. Choosing the method
step5.ok: Correct method. Once you move on, steps 1–4 become read-only.
step5.why: Choose a method and write a justification (5+ words)

step6.title: Step 6. Analysis in R or Python
step6.introPost: Write the analysis code yourself — it really runs, right in your browser. The case data file is already attached.
step6.introPre: Fill in the blanks in the template and run the code — it really runs, right in your browser.
step6.phoneOnly: Only Python is available on a phone
step6.phoneNote: Only Python is available on a phone. We recommend a computer for this step: both R and Python are available there and coding is easier. Your work is saved — you can continue on a computer.
step6.otherLang: The other language ({{lang}}) opens for comparison after the case is finished.
step6.why: The code must run without errors
step6.loadingPython: Loading Python into your browser. The first time takes up to a minute, after that a few seconds.
step6.loadingR: Loading R into your browser. The first time takes 1–2 minutes (a computer and internet are needed), after that a few seconds.
step6.wrongAnalysis: The code ran, but it does not analyse what the case question needs: check which variables and which method you use.
step6.timeout: The code ran too long and was stopped. Check for an infinite loop and run it again.
step6.simulatedNote: R/Python could not be loaded (check your internet) — a pre-computed result is shown. The step is counted.

step7.title: Step 7. Interpretation
step7.intro: Write the conclusion in your own words. The tutor does not write it for you at this step.
step7.label: Your conclusion
step7.structure: Structure of the conclusion (no ready-made wording):

step8.title: Step 8. Critical check of AI
step8.intro: Another AI wrote a conclusion from these data. Click the fragment with an error and explain what is correct. The tutor is not available at this step.
step8.label: What is wrong and what is correct
step8.why: Choose a fragment and write a correction (5+ words)

step9.title: Step 9. Debriefing
step9.disputed: Disputed · the score is preliminary, you can continue
step9.dialogIntro: Your answer, the AI score and your arguments go to the study author or an assigned teacher. Until the decision the score is “disputed”, but you can keep learning. The decision and its justification will appear here.
step9.argumentPh: Why you disagree with the score

step10.title: Step 10. Case completed
step10.resultNote: , preliminary. You will be notified of the teacher's decision in the app and by e-mail.
step10.otherCode: The {{lang}} code is now available for comparison:
step10.note: The next case is not filled in the prototype — the button goes to the home page.

debrief.method1: Method chosen on the first attempt
debrief.method2: Method chosen on the second attempt
debrief.interpMissing: The conclusion is missing required elements

review.intro: Disputed scores first. A dispute does not block the student; they will see the decision and its justification.

people.footer: Exports contain participant codes only. The “code — name” table is kept separately by the study author.

import.title: Add participants
import.help: A CSV file from Excel with columns code;role;group;lang, e.g. P-1001;student;KZ-301;kk. Role: student, specialist or teacher. Language: kk, ru or en. No names — codes only. Existing participants are not changed.
import.passwordsHelp: Download the file and hand the passwords out. A lost password can be reissued with the “New password” button.

reset.confirm: The old password will stop working.

editor.intro: A case is published only after the key is checked by a biostatistician and the content by a medical education expert. The author decides on publication.
editor.newIntro: The draft is saved automatically. Before submitting for review you can open the case as a student.
editor.name: Title
editor.namePh: e.g. Missed ART doses and viral suppression
editor.situationPh: The learner's role and professional task
editor.dataHint: The “Training data” label is added automatically. Real names of territories and organisations are not used.

diagTab.intro: Students take variant A (entry) themselves at their first login. You open variant B (final) at the end of the pilot, for each group separately. Students will see an invitation on their home page.
diagTab.empty: You have no groups with students yet.
diagTab.confirm: Open the final diagnostic for group {{group}}? Open it at the end of the pilot, once students have done the cases.
diagTab.note: Results of both variants are in the Analytics tab and in the “Diagnostic · CSV” export (variant column: A or B).

group.title: Create a group
group.intro: Codes (P-1001, P-1002…) and passwords are issued automatically. After creating, print the cards and hand them out in class.
group.name: Group
group.orCsv: or upload a ready list from CSV

issued.cardNote: You can change the password in your profile after signing in.

scope.mine: Your groups: {{groups}}. You see and export only these.
scope.none: No groups are assigned to you yet — contact the lead teacher.
scope.all: You are the lead teacher: you see all groups. Other teachers see only the groups assigned to them.
scope.howTo: New teachers are created and assigned groups by the system administrator.

nav.label: Sections
nav.privacy: Training data — no personal medical data

overview.lead: Learn biostatistics through practice cases. The AI tutor asks questions, guides your reasoning and helps you check your conclusion — but the decision is yours.
overview.routeTitle: From a question to a justified conclusion
overview.routeLead: One cycle develops biostatistical, analytical and AI competence.

diag.title: Diagnostic
diag.text: Baseline level across four competencies and areas for growth.

practice.title: Practice
practice.text: 10-step cases on training medical data, R and Python code.

critical.title: Critical check
critical.text: Find errors in AI answers and justify your decision.

reflection.title: Reflection
reflection.text: Debriefing after each case and competency dynamics.

casesPage.title: Learn from medical data
casesPage.lead: Each case goes from a research question to a professional conclusion. The data are simulated specifically for training.

tutorPage.title: AI tutor
tutorPage.lead: Describe a statistical task. The tutor does not give a ready answer right away — it first helps you clarify the data and the logic of choosing a method.
tutorPage.principle: AI guides the reasoning but does not replace your own analysis. Check its recommendations.
tutorPage.how3: Come back to AI-Biostat — your progress is saved
tutorPage.blocked: Inside a case the tutor is closed at the Question, Interpretation and AI check steps — you work on your own there.
tutorPage.privacy: Do not send patients' personal data to the tutor. Visits to the tutor are counted for the study (count only).
tutorPage.examplesLead: Copy a question and paste it into the tutor window.
examples: I need to compare two groups. Where do I start choosing a method?
How do I tell what type my variable is?
When should I use the χ² test and when Fisher's exact test?
How do the median and mean differ, and when should I report each?
How do I phrase a conclusion without causal claims?

analysis.title: R and Python module
analysis.lead: Upload an anonymised CSV file or use the training dataset. The system calculates descriptive statistics and shows reproducible R and Python code.
analysis.privacy: Do not upload names or other personal data. The file is processed only in your browser and is not sent to the server.
analysis.readError: Could not read the CSV file. Check that the first row contains column names.
analysis.tooBig: The file is larger than 5 MB — use part of the data for this training module.
analysis.detectedCategorical: Detected as categorical — a frequency table will be shown.
analysis.empty: Here you will see the number of observations, mean, standard deviation, median, quartiles, minimum and maximum — or a frequency table for a categorical variable.
analysis.catFooter: n = {{n}}, missing: {{missing}}. Percentages are of non-missing values.
analysis.moreLevels: Showing the 30 most frequent of {{n}} values.
analysis.numericHint: Write the interpretation yourself: central tendency and spread. Look at the minimum and maximum — are there impossible values (data entry errors)?
analysis.categoricalHint: Describe which categories prevail. Check whether one category is written in different ways (e.g. Cyrillic «М» and Latin «M»).
analysis.codeHint: The same calculation in R or Python. Quantiles are computed the same way as here (R default, pandas), so the numbers will match.

aicheck.title: Find the statistical error
aicheck.lead: Rate the AI statement, then justify your decision. This is a trainer — it does not affect case scores.
aicheck.reasonPh: Explain: what data are involved, what the AI claims and why it is right or wrong…

outcome.ok: Correct. Your rating and justification are accepted.
outcome.wrongVerdict: The rating is not accurate yet. Identify the data type and check whether the AI statement fits such data.
outcome.tooShort: The rating is correct — now justify it in more detail (at least {{min}} words).
outcome.weakReason: The rating is correct, but the key point is missing: name the data type, the appropriate method or what is missing for the conclusion.

aicheck.footer: Answers are saved. The explanation appears after a correct answer or after the second attempt.

progress.title: My progress
progress.lead: Your results in cases and the trainer. Only you and your teacher can see them.
progress.preliminary: AI score is preliminary until the teacher's decision
progress.dynamicsLead: Entry diagnostic and results in completed cases across the same four competencies.
progress.noCasesYet: The result in cases will appear after your first completed case (with debriefing).
progress.footer: The final diagnostic (variant B) will be at the end of the pilot — then a before/after comparison will appear.

analytics.title: Group learning analytics
analytics.lead: Aggregated indicators without personal data and without ranking students.
analytics.testGroup: The data include the test group «ТЕСТ». To keep it from skewing the figures, choose a specific group.
analytics.noWeak: All steps are at 80% or higher.

advice.data: Finding data errors: impossible values, sign, coding.
advice.types: Variable types and choosing the outcome.
advice.question: Formulating the research question.
advice.method: Choosing a method: outcome type, number of groups, independence.
advice.code: R / Python code: column names, running without a hint.
advice.interp: Interpretation: proportions, statistic and p, direction, limitations.

analytics.compLead: Average of the entry diagnostic (completed: {{n}}) and of case results.
analytics.footer: Final grading remains with the teacher. Data export for the study is in the «Participants and export» tab.
analytics.compExit: Took the final one: {{n}} — the bars show “entry → final”.
